title: Frontend: Stopwatch
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Stopwatch. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Start, Pause, Tick and Reset buttons drive an injected one-second clock. Tick increases [data-testid="seconds"] only while running. Start is idempotent, Pause retains elapsed time, Reset stops and clears. This deterministic clock adapter omits real timer scheduling.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a monotonic clock for elapsed duration, storing accumulated time and the current run’s start timestamp.
alternativeApproaches: Add lap times and verify that background-tab throttling does not cause elapsed time to drift.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Start/pause/resume; reset; delayed interval.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
